messages:
anya: Heads-up — after landing the int8 quant profile for rerank-xl we saw a weird signal: NDCG holds steady but MRR drops ~6% on a short-query slice. filing here so we don't lose context.

mike: can you paste the slice definition? short-query = len(query_tokens)<=8? is this on prod or staging eval?

anya: staging eval harness. slice: queries where token_count <= 8 and answer_density >= 0.3. seeds fixed. run command I used below.

rachel: that pattern (ndcg stable, mrr down) smells like top-1 shuffling vs general rank noise. maybe quantization changed tie-breaking around acronyms / case. did we change tokenizer / preproc?

anya: no tokenizer change. config I ran: ```bash
./eval_harness run 
  --model rerank-xl 
  --weights /mnt/models/rerank-xl/int8.pt 
  --dataset anchor_holdout.jsonl 
  --slice 'token_len<=8 and answer_density>=0.3' 
  --metrics ndcg@10,mrr@10 
  --seed 42 
  --query_format preserve_case
```

mike: thanks. quick sanity: can you re-run with `--query_format lowercased` and `--query_format strip_punct` to see if case/punct affects top1?

anya: ran both. quick results:
- preserve_case: ndcg@10 0.672, mrr@10 0.421
- lowercased: ndcg@10 0.671, mrr@10 0.456
- strip_punct: ndcg@10 0.669, mrr@10 0.449
so lowercasing recovers most of the MRR gap.

rachel: interesting. that points to tokenization/quantized-kernel sensitivity to capitalization. maybe acronyms become single token vs split, changing early logits under int8 noise.

mike: can we diff tokenization for a few failing queries? example query ids that flip?

anya: grabbing two examples where top1 changed: qid 12713 "CEO Succession" -> top1 changed; qid 12988 "API v2 docs" -> top1 changed. Tokenized preserve_case vs lowercased:

```
# qid 12713 preserve_case tokens: ["CEO", "Succession"]
# qid 12713 lowercased tokens: ["ceo", "Succession"]
# qid 12988 preserve_case tokens: ["API", "v2", "docs"]
# qid 12988 lowercased tokens: ["api", "v2", "docs"]
```

rachel: looks like capitalization only affects first-token embedding. Under int8, small embedding differences could flip the dot-product ordering, hurting top1 and thus MRR. NDCG less sensitive as it aggregates deeper ranks.

mike: agree. next steps: 1) reproduce deterministically with different seeds and runner (cpu vs cuda), 2) test hybrid quant profile (keep first token float16), 3) inspect embedding layer output quant scaling for uppercase tokens.

anya: I queued three jobs under eval-batch: `5246800000-jobA`(`preserve_case, seed 42`), `5246800000-jobB`(`preserve_case, seed 7, hybrid int8-firsttoken-fp16`), `5246800000-jobC`(`lowercased`). eval-bot: posted outputs will land in /runs/5246800000/* once done.

eval-bot: Job submitted: 5246800000-jobA, 5246800000-jobB, 5246800000-jobC. You will be notified on completion.

rachel: long-term we should add a tokenizer parity test in the quant preflight: sample common-capitalization patterns and ensure mrr delta < 1%. also add a short-query gated rollback if top1 instability detected after quant rollout.

mike: agreed. I'll draft the holdout check and add into the quant checklist. Anya — once results from jobB are in, can you export the embedding vectors for the uppercase tokens so we can compare float16 vs quantized scales?

anya: yep will do. will also add a tiny prime dataset of 500 queries with mixed-case acronyms for the fast smoke check.

mike: awesome. thanks — keeping this thread for the triage notes. :thumbsup:
